relativity.definition: the study of objects moving at speeds greater than about 1% of the speed of light, or of objects being affected by a strong gravitational field
the study of how different observers measure the same event

quantum mechanics.definition: the study of objects smaller than can be seen with a microscope
the branch of physics that deals with small objects and with the quantization of various entities, especially energy

power.definition: the rate at which work is done

oscillate.section: Introduction to Oscillatory Motion and Waves
oscillate.definition: moving back and forth regularly between two points

oscillate.section: Production and Properties of Electromagnetic Waves
oscillate.definition: to fluctuate back and forth in a steady beat

frequency.definition: number of events per unit of time

frequency.section: Production and Properties of Electromagnetic Waves
frequency.definition: the number of complete wave cycles (up-down-up) passing a given point within one second (cycles/second)

amplitude.section: Simple Harmonic Motion: A Special Periodic Motion
amplitude.definition: the maximum displacement from the equilibrium position of an object oscillating around the equilibrium position

amplitude.section: Production and Properties of Electromagnetic Waves
amplitude.definition: the height, or magnitude, of an electromagnetic wave

transverse wave.definition: a wave in which the disturbance is perpendicular to the direction of propagation

transverse wave.section: Production and Properties of Electromagnetic Waves
transverse wave.definition: a wave, such as an electromagnetic wave, which oscillates perpendicular to the axis along the line of travel

wavelength.definition: the distance between adjacent identical parts of a wave

wavelength.section: Production and Properties of Electromagnetic Waves
wavelength.definition: the distance from one peak to the next in a wave

electric field.definition: a three-dimensional map of the electric force extended out into space from a point charge

electric field.section: Production and Properties of Electromagnetic Waves
electric field.definition: a vector quantity (E); the lines of electric force per unit charge, moving radially outward from a positive charge and in toward a negative charge

electric field lines.definition: a series of lines drawn from a point charge representing the magnitude and direction of force exerted by that charge

electric field lines.section: Maxwell’s Equations: Electromagnetic Waves Predicted and Observed
electric field lines.definition: a pattern of imaginary lines that extend between an electric source and charged objects in the surrounding area, with arrows pointed away from positively charged objects and toward negatively charged objects. The more lines in the pattern, the stronger the electric field in that region

polarized.definition: a state in which the positive and negative charges within an object have collected in separate locations
waves having the electric and magnetic field oscillations in a definite direction

magnetic field.section: Magnetic Fields and Magnetic Field Lines
Production and Properties of Electromagnetic Waves
magnetic field.definition: a vector quantity (B); can be used to determine the magnetic force on a moving charged particle

magnetic field lines.section: Magnetic Fields and Magnetic Field Lines
magnetic field lines.definition: the pictorial representation of the strength and the direction of a magnetic field

magnetic field lines.section: Maxwell’s Equations: Electromagnetic Waves Predicted and Observed
magnetic field lines.definition: a pattern of continuous, imaginary lines that emerge from and enter into opposite magnetic poles. The density of the lines indicates the magnitude of the magnetic field

maxwell’s equations.section: Magnetic Fields Produced by Currents: Ampere’s Law
maxwell’s equations.definition: a set of four equations that describe electromagnetic phenomena

maxwell’s equations.section: Maxwell’s Equations: Electromagnetic Waves Predicted and Observed
maxwell’s equations.definition: a set of four equations that comprise a complete, overarching theory of electromagnetism

gamma ray.definition: electromagnetic radiation emitted in nuclear transitions; in astronomy, the term also includes very high-energy photons produced by other processes
a component of nuclear radioactivity; consists of a high-energy photon

gluons.definition: the eight types of particles that carry the strong interaction between quarks. Gluons themselves carry color charge and can interact with one another
the eight types of particles that carry the strong interaction between quarks. Gluons themselves carry color charge and can interact with one another
